children: The Indian rupee weakened modestly on Thursday, weighed by elevated oil prices due to the deepening Middle East conflict, with anticipated outflows also adding to the strain, contained by likely intervention.
dipped 0.2% to 95.30 per dollar, its weakest level in about 10 days as oil prices marched higher after Iran and the U.S. hit tankers in the biggest wave of attacks on shipping since the war began.
State-run banks were spotted offering dollars in the 95.30-95.35 range, most likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, three traders said.
Such dollar sales from state-run banks occurred over multiple trading sessions last week, limiting the rupee's fall despite lingering pressures.

On the day, heightened demand to buy dollars at the daily reference rate, flows linked to corporates' overseas debt repayments and hedging demand from local importers also troubled the currency, traders said.
"The intensity of RBI interventions has diminished over last two-three sessions, so 95.50 could be on the cards sooner rather than later," a trader at a state-run bank said.
lingered just shy of the 99 mark while Asian currencies were trading mixed. Stocks in Asia were under pressure as well with the MSCI's gauge of regional stocks down 0.5%.
Higher oil prices and elevated bond yields have weighed on investor sentiment, setting the stage for the series of central bank meetings in the coming days.
The European Central Bank is expected to raise rates later today while the U.S. Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan will deliver policy decisions next week.

"While higher inflation may warrant tighter policy, additional rate hikes would also increase government borrowing costs at a time when fiscal deficits and debt servicing burdens are already under scrutiny," MUFG said in a note.
